nodes.title: Verify read-only mode is actually active, by real chat
nodes.notes: Earlier: real KiroCrew ask turns and a read-only tool observation existed, but did not prove same-session identity, safe detach or cross-host integration. 2026-11-04 source reading found the read-only claim was ADVERTISED, not enforced: the shim forwarded session/prompt verbatim and upstream answers -32601 for session/set_mode, so the mode never reached the daemon (phenotype-registry 09_READ_ONLY_ENFORCEMENT_GAP.md). Fixed forward in 8c2adb1: prompts are now refused by default with -32012 and only forwarded under an explicit --allow-prompt-forwarding, at which point capabilities honestly flip readOnly=false. So read-only is now enforced AT THE SHIM BOUNDARY. What remains UNPROVEN is end-to-end: KiroCrew narrows a static tool allowlist and uses session/request_permission, while jcode arbitrates a live interaction lease; the shim does not bridge those models, so the daemon's own tool authority is unchanged whenever a prompt is forwarded. P6 stays UNKNOWN for the end-to-end claim only.

nodes.notes: Cross-host end-to-end integration is still not proven. 2026-11-04 evidence narrows it precisely: a REAL Kiro Crew agent turn dispatched tool kiro-inventory/agent_sources (structured row in ~/.kiro/crew/sessions/dashboard_chat-2-1793781242.jsonl with meta.input, meta.done=true) but returned "Error: MCP server 'kiro-inventory' not connected", and a later turn reported "Connected MCP servers: 0 (0 tools)". So DISPATCH is observed and EXECUTION failed. Cause identified in edcc513: agent sessions run the codex ACP backend and Crew composes session/new.mcpServers only from ~/.kiro/agents/<name>.json (acp/session_mcp.py:1-9,:368,:1472); the previously edited ~/.kiro/crew/mcp.json is dashboard projection read by nothing on the session path, and kiro-inventory appears in 0 of 17 agent specs. Also unproven: why kirocrew-core/cron also connect 0 tools. 2026-11-04 follow-up: the desktop is not the blocker. See P16 for the five measured findings and the one missing observation (session/new.mcpServers payload). Dispatch was observed once on the dashboard path; execution has never been observed on any path.

nodes.title: Validate the Windows CIM assumptions against the real desk host
nodes.notes: All six assumptions CONFIRMED on desk, none refuted. LastBootUpTime returned 2026-11-03T03:39:42.6681070Z (7 fractional digits, matches the parser regex). A single matching pid yields a single JSON OBJECT with pid/creation/executable. A filter matching nothing yields empty stdout with exit 0 (the empty-result case, not a failure). ExecutablePath is null for 28 of 1385 processes, which the parser drops and the policy then refuses - correct fail-closed. powershell.exe 5.1.28000.3393 wins the resolution order. The UTF-8 preamble is load-bearing: with it a non-ASCII path survives as 16 high bytes; without it, eight literal '?' appear. Also noted: -EncodedCommand would emit CLIXML to stderr, which this module treats as a failed read - a trap for any future transport change, not a current defect.

nodes.title: Give Windows a real per-boot epoch so CIM identity can be placed on it
nodes.notes: Reads Win32_OperatingSystem.LastBootUpTime once per process run through the same bounded _run_capture path, cached, and returns unknown on any failure (missing shell, stderr, truncation, timeout, stalled reader, malformed text). Every failure is cached as unknown so the answer cannot change mid-run. same_process now requires boot epoch + exact pid + CIM creation time (cim-creation: prefix) + executable path together; unknown boot refuses on both sides. Composition proven by synthetic tests only.

nodes.title: Prove live adoption of a specific externally-started session, with detach
nodes.notes: First real attached run against an externally-started daemon, entirely inside two disposable scratch roots (HOME and JCODE_HOME redirected, socket asserted inside scratch before start, JCODE_NO_TELEMETRY=1). Session session_palmtree_1793781570983_6ba126eb93a04965 created on the isolated daemon; session/load forwarded that exact id and returned the daemon's configOptions; session/new answered -32601; session/close returned {closed:false, detached:true}; the session file was byte-identical (SHA256_BEFORE == SHA256_AFTER) immediately after detach; two later ACP clients re-loaded the same session, so detach neither cancelled nor closed it; serve-process count was unchanged (2 -> 2), so adoption spawned no daemon. Only the two scratch PIDs were signalled, each re-verified by matching its command line to its own scratch socket. The synthetic probe remains the regression gate (27 checks).

nodes.title: Make the read-only claim true at the shim boundary
nodes.notes: session/prompt is refused locally with -32012 SHIM_PROMPT_FORWARDING_DISABLED plus structured data, checked after the adoption precondition and before any upstream call. Forwarding requires the explicit --allow-prompt-forwarding flag, and capabilities then flip readOnly=false / promptForwarding=true so the advertisement matches reality. session/cancel is local while prompting is disabled. Unchanged: session/new blocked at the transport, session/close never forwarded, write-config refusal, and the two-probe adoption gate. Residual, documented in docs/ACP-ADOPTION-SHIM.md: once a prompt IS forwarded the daemon's own tool authority is unenforceable.

nodes.title: Bridge KiroCrew's static allowlist onto jcode's live interaction lease
nodes.notes: The remaining reason a forwarded prompt is not contained. Kiro Crew derives and narrows a static tool allowlist and drives permission through session/request_permission; jcode arbitrates a live per-session interaction lease (require_interaction_ownership, src/cli/acp/interactions.rs). The shim is a passthrough and maps neither onto the other. This is a design project, not a flag. Until it exists, 'read-only' is a shim-boundary property only.

nodes.title: Wire the read-only inventory server into the agent spec that sessions read
nodes.notes: Four verification attempts, all NOT PROVEN. Chain of findings, each measured: (1) ~/.kiro/crew/mcp.json is dashboard projection only - the session path never reads it (edcc513). (2) Crew's own composer DOES mount the entry: @kiro-inventory resolved and is absent from the unresolved list (docs/mcp-mount-predicate.md), so the absence is decided downstream, in the harness's own config merge. (3) The launcher died under the empty environment codex gives MCP children - 'HOME: unbound variable' - so the server never started and Crew surfaced nothing; fixed in 887a79b and verified under env -i. (4) The MCP set the agent actually reported (portal-bridge, workos-docs, node_repl, phinbox-mcp) matches ~/.codex/config.toml, so [mcp_servers.kiro-inventory] was added there (backup config.toml.bak-20261104T011421) and codex mcp list shows it enabled. (5) Still no call: a 153s turn ended with the model itself saying the server is not configured or connected, and the audit file never appeared. Instrument now in place: opt-in server-side attestation (5d167bd, KIRO_INVENTORY_AUDIT_LOG, one redacted line per call, 478 tests pass) plus that env registered in codex config (76e3dd0). A direct invocation writes {tool: agent_sources, ok: true, result_bytes: 527}, so the instrument works - the turn never reaches the server. MISSING OBSERVATION, and the next step: capture the actual session/new.mcpServers payload for one turn. Without it, whether the array omits the entry or the transport drops it is UNKNOWN. Do not claim integration on configuration. FINAL 2026-11-04T23:54Z: CODEX-SIDE DELIVERY PROVEN. Invoking codex directly (not through Crew) produced an audit line: {"tool": "agent_sources", "ok": true, "result_bytes": 527} (docs/codex-mcp-reachability.md, commit 4ca13c9). So the config entry, the env table, the launcher and the attestation all work end to end. Combined with providers/mirrors/codex.py:578 - 'Crew writes no codex file today', i.e. there is NO Crew-owned CODEX_HOME overlay - the remaining hypothesis is that Crew's session/new.mcpServers array REPLACES codex-acp's own ~/.codex config rather than merging with it, so an entry that works for plain codex never reaches a Crew session. NEXT STEP, one observation: capture that array. If it omits kiro-inventory, the fix is in Crew's projection; if it contains it, the fix is in how codex-acp merges the two.

nodes.title: Fix the Windows boot epoch on the real host
nodes.notes: CLOSED AND PROVEN ON HARDWARE. Two independent defects, both invisible to the mocked suite because both lived in the REQUEST rather than the answer. (1) _windows_boot.py concatenated the brace-escaped _POWERSHELL_PREAMBLE without calling .format(); PowerShell treats {{ }} as a nested script block and emits its text to stdout, so output was two lines and the single-line guard rejected it, leaving boot_id() unknown. (2) windows_liveness ran `tasklist -NH` without -FO CSV yet parsed rows as CSV, so every row was skipped, every liveness answer was UNKNOWN and describe_many dropped every pid - which only surfaced after (1) was fixed, because before that the code never reached the liveness check. Measured on desk after both fixes: boot_id is cim-boot:2026-11-03T03:39:42.6681070Z; describe_many bound 2 of 2; start_identity is a subsecond cim-creation; same_process(own) True; wrong pid, exe, start and boot all refused. The identity and boot suites ran on the host: 56 tests OK, including the 3 that used to fail for fixture-portability reasons, now built from the product's own platform predicate.

nodes.title: Make the desk posture reversible
nodes.notes: The defect is irreversibility, not the choice: the installer runs setx and rewrites agent.acp_backend, and there is no uninstaller and no documented setx removal. Delivering uninstall-kirocrew-jcode-backend.ps1 (dry-run, backup, .NET SetEnvironmentVariable to null rather than setx), a -RevertCheck, and README-rollback.md. Recommendation recorded: fail closed on Windows via sandbox_allow_unsandboxed_exec=false and keep jcode-on-KiroCrew only where a real OS sandbox backend exists (macOS). Not executed against desk; no PowerShell on this Mac, so reviewed-only unless proven otherwise.
